slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Theorem: the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

Proof: let the diagonals of parallelogram ABCD meet at M. AB = CD (opposite sides), angle BAM = angle DCM and angle ABM = angle CDM (alternate interior angles). So triangle ABM is congruent to triangle CDM by ASA, and AM = CM, BM = DM.

So M is the midpoint of both diagonals, and a 180 degree rotation about M maps the parallelogram onto itself: a parallelogram has point symmetry.
